class.name: NetwSceneCore
class.brief_description: The scene column's record plane: which scenes are live, a routing table keyed by scene identity, and the one scene request in flight.
class.description: It references no [Node] and instantiates nothing, which is what makes a registration outlive the scene it names. The one node it names, the spawn anchor, it holds as an instance id resolved at each read rather than as a reference, so a freed anchor is no anchor and nothing here keeps a node alive. A scene is identified by the entity [RID] it is keyed under rather than by whichever node is currently standing in for it, so rebuilding a scene does not silently drop everyone watching it. It mints no scene identity of its own; every [RID] arrives from whatever the liveness plane keys scenes under. Everything that mounts, frees or instantiates a [Node] or a [PackedScene] lives in the interface above this class, which is why the anchor is a decision here and a parenting act there. [codeblock] scene_enter(scene, stem) the book gains a live scene under a non-unique stem scene_named(stem) an instance of that stem scenes_named(stem) every instance of it, in registration order scene_retire(scene, pumps) out of the book now, out of memory after the drain set_scene_anchor(node) what a declaration node parents its scenes under spawn_anchor(fallback) that anchor while it lives, the fallback otherwise observe(scene, event, callback) one row per (event, scene), in registration order dispatch(scene, event, ...) every live callback; the dead ones are dropped here open_request() the next id, and it becomes the pending one request_open(from_capture) supersedes what was in flight, answers a promise is_current(id) whether a reply names the request still in flight request_settle(id, code) settles that promise and lets go, in one act request_abandon(code) settles whatever is in flight, at teardown declaration_open(...) a draft nobody can read yet declaration_row(stem, ...) one declared scene into that draft declaration_publish() the draft becomes the declaration, at once [/codeblock] The session's scene declaration is held here as detached rows rather than as the authoring resource it came from, which is what makes an authoring edit after the fact impossible to make silently: the only way to change what a session declares is to publish a new draft over the old one. A stem names an archetype and not an instance, so two live copies of one level share one. [method scene_named] answers with the one that entered most recently, and losing it promotes the oldest survivor sharing the stem rather than making the stem unanswerable. A request id can only be drawn, never claimed. There is no setter for [member pending_request_id], because an id a caller could assign without opening would let it answer a request nobody made. The request protocol's decisions live here as well. [method verify_requested_path] bounds what a peer may name and [method admits_request] is the consent line a request clears on its own, both static verbs over their arguments, and both refusals a caller can check rather than crashes it has to avoid. [method decide_request] is the one verdict composed from them: [member request_handler] answers when one is installed, that consent line when none is.

method.name: clear
method.description: Forgets the live book, every registration and the request record, and restarts the id counter. Session teardown.

method.name: close_request
method.description: Clears [member pending_request_id], so a second reply for the same request finds nothing rather than answering one that already answered.

method.name: dispatch
method.description: Calls every live callback registered for [param scene] under [param event], in registration order, passing [param present] and [param subject]. Returns how many were called. A callback whose object is gone is dropped here rather than at a sweep somebody has to remember to run, because a dispatch is the only moment the row is already being walked. A callback is arbitrary code and may register another observer, so the walk runs over a copy of the row taken before it starts. Anything registered during the walk is kept: the pruning is entitled to drop what it found dead, not to roll the row back to what it saw.

method.name: forget_scene
method.description: Drops every registration on [param scene], across every event. A scene that is gone routes nothing.

method.name: is_current
method.description: Returns whether [param request_id] is the request currently in flight. A [param request_id] of zero is never current, so a settled request cannot be settled a second time.

method.name: observe
method.description: Registers [param callback] for [param event] on [param scene]. An invalid [param scene] or an unset [param callback] registers nothing, so a later [method dispatch] can never find a row nobody meant to create. Registering the same [param callback] twice stores it once, so an edge is heard once. [param event] is a raw ordinal mirroring a GDScript enum this tier cannot see, kept in sync by value rather than by name.

method.name: observer_count
method.description: How many callbacks one row holds, counting any whose object has died since the last [method dispatch] reached them.

method.name: open_request
method.description: Draws the next request id, makes it the pending one, and returns it. Ids come from one counter, so a reply can name the request it answers and a stale reply can be told apart from the current one.

method.name: scene_enter
method.description: Records [param scene] as live under [param stem], and makes it the instance [method scene_named] answers with. Entering a scene already in the book re-stems it rather than doubling it. [param owns_its_world] is what [method would_share_one_world] reads.

method.name: scene_exit
method.description: Drops [param scene] from the book. When it was the instance its stem answered with, the oldest survivor sharing that stem takes the answer, so retiring one arena does not make the other unreachable by name.

method.name: scene_retire
method.description: [method scene_exit], and then a drain window of [param drain_pumps] pumps before [method pump_retired] hands [param scene] back to be freed. The window is counted in pumps because what it holds open is an address for frames still in flight, and the pump is what carries them.

method.name: pump_retired
method.description: Advances every drain window by one pump and returns the scenes whose window closed, dropping them. Empty when nothing is retiring or nothing is due.

method.name: retiring_scenes
method.description: Every scene still inside its drain window. A session that ends has no next pump, so its teardown reads this rather than waiting for one.

method.name: resolve_current
method.description: What this peer presents, given whether it presents anything at all and which scene the session seats it in. The answer is what [member current_scene] is set from; it is not stored by this call. [codeblock] presents is false -> an invalid RID, whatever is live seat is valid -> the seat, even when it is not in the book otherwise -> the first live scene its stem answers with [/codeblock] [param presents] is false for a dedicated server, which runs every live scene and stands in none of them. Presentation is a local act and the role that decides it is the session's, so it arrives as a reading rather than being looked up here. The fallback skips a scene its stem no longer answers with, so a session holding two instances of one level presents the instance [method scene_named] names rather than whichever entered first.

method.name: is_live
method.description: Whether [param scene] is in the book. False for one that retired, whose wrapper may still be draining.

method.name: scene_named
method.description: An instance of [param stem], or an invalid [RID]. See [method scenes_named] when the difference between an instance and every one of them matters.

method.name: scenes_named
method.description: Every live scene whose stem is [param stem], in registration order.

method.name: live_scenes
method.description: Every live scene, in registration order.

method.name: live_count
method.description: How many scenes are live.

method.name: would_share_one_world
method.description: Whether a scene arriving now would land in a physics space another live scene is already simulating in, which is true exactly when at least one scene is live and none of them declared a world of its own. Legal, and usually a mistake, so it is what the interface warns on.

method.name: stem_of
method.description: The stem [param scene] entered under, or an empty [StringName] when it is not live.

method.name: request_open
method.description: Supersedes whatever request was in flight with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_SKIP], draws the next id, and answers the promise that request will settle through. [param from_capture] records that the request began as a captured native scene change, which is what decides whether [signal native_change_settled] announces its outcome. The promise is minted here rather than handed in, because a request nobody opened is one nothing can answer.

method.name: request_settle
method.description: Settles the request in flight when [param request_id] names it, resolving the promise on [constant @GlobalScope.OK] and rejecting it on anything else, and answers whether it did. One act, because checking the id and letting go of the request are two chances to do one without the other, and either half alone answers a request twice or never lets go of one.

method.name: request_abandon
method.description: Settles whatever is in flight with [param code], whatever its id. Session teardown, where there is no answer coming and a promise nobody settles is one a caller awaits forever.

method.name: receive_result_frame
method.description: Settles the request in flight from a server-authored result frame, and answers whether it did. A [param sender] other than the server authors nothing, and a payload that is not a two-element [Array] of id and code settles nothing, because a request arrives off the wire and a frame nobody checked is a frame a peer chooses.

method.name: transition_open
method.description: Claims the single slot a whole-session replacement holds, and answers whether it was free. A second transition entered while one is still moving peers is refused here, so concurrent approvals never interleave moves against a half-transitioned roster. Asking and claiming are one act. Two calls would let one caller read the slot free and take it after another caller already had it.

method.name: transition_arm
method.description: Records what the claimed transition is: the scene everyone ends up in, the scenes they are leaving, and the one answer the whole transition owes. Call it once, after [method transition_open] answered [code]true[/code] and the target actually exists. The record is a cursor rather than a loop because a pending move is subscribed to rather than awaited, so the walk has to be resumable. Every walk verb below reads and advances this one record. [codeblock] if not core.transition_open(): promise.reject(ERR_UNAVAILABLE) return core.transition_arm(target, sources, promise) [/codeblock]

method.name: transition_target
method.description: The scene the armed transition moves everyone into, or [code]null[/code] once the transition has left through [method transition_land], [method transition_fail] or [method transition_close].

method.name: transition_sources
method.description: The scenes the armed transition is emptying, in the order [method transition_arm] took them. They are the scenes the caller retires once every participant has landed.

method.name: transition_next_mover
method.description: The next participant the transition still owes a move, or [code]null[/code] when every source is walked. [param roster_of] answers the participants inside one source. It is called when the walk REACHES that source and never ahead of it, so a peer that left during an earlier source's moves is gone from the roster before it is asked to move. A caller that flattened every roster up front would pin a roster taken before the first move. [codeblock] sources: [A, B] take A -> roster_of(A) -> [p1, p2] p1, p2 handed out take B -> roster_of(B) -> [p3] p3 handed out no sources left -> null [/codeblock]

method.name: transition_accept
method.description: Records one arrived mover, or ends the whole transition on its rejection, and answers whether the walk may continue. A [param code] other than [constant @GlobalScope.OK] rejects the armed promise as [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] through [method transition_fail], so the first failure aborts rather than the walk carrying on against a roster it can no longer complete.

method.name: transition_moved
method.description: Whether [param peer] was carried into the target by a move [method transition_accept] recorded. Everyone else is admitted on landing instead.

method.name: transition_fail
method.description: Releases the slot and rejects the armed promise with [param code]. A participant left outside the destination would present a scene it is not in, so a partial transition fails here rather than half-landing.

method.name: transition_land
method.description: Releases the slot and resolves the armed promise. Call it last, because it drops the record [method transition_sources] and [method transition_target] answer from.

method.name: transition_close
method.description: Releases the slot [method transition_open] claimed and drops the record [method transition_arm] wrote, without answering the promise. Idempotent, because the transition unwinds down several paths and each of them releases a slot it may not have taken. Every path out of a transition passes through here, which is what keeps a refused or abandoned change from holding the slot shut.

method.name: native_entry_verdict
method.description: What a marked scene entering the tree natively becomes on this peer, as one [enum Capture]. The whole input is the local presentation state, so the same table answers on a client, a dedicated server and a listen host without any of them holding a rule of its own. [codeblock] no path -> CAPTURE_REFUSED not the server -> CAPTURE_REQUEST session reach, a scene already live -> CAPTURE_CHANGE_SESSION a listen host inside its own world -> CAPTURE_MOVE_ME otherwise -> CAPTURE_ACTIVATE [/codeblock]

method.name: decide_request
method.description: One player scene request's single verdict. [member request_handler] answers when one is installed, called as [code](participant, destination, args)[/code]; with none installed the reading falls to [method admits_request] over [param named], [param marked], [param gated] and [param path]. A request has exactly one verdict, which is why the door is a single owner rather than a veto every listener may raise: several listeners disagreeing over one request has no defined resolution. A handler that answers anything but a number has answered no verdict at all, and that refuses. Otherwise [constant @GlobalScope.OK] admits and every other code refuses, so a handler cannot admit by returning something truthy. [param named], [param marked] and [param gated] are readings the authoring tier owns and are handed in already decided, because the registry answering whether a script is a marked scene stays GDScript.

method.name: admits_request
method.description: The consent line one player scene request clears when no request handler is installed. A declared name or a marked scene admits, a raw unmarked path does not, and a gated or session-wide mark denies either. A [param path] that bounded to nothing is admitted by nothing, since there is no destination left to move to.

method.name: verify_requested_path
method.description: Returns [param path] when it names a scene file a peer may request, and an empty [String] otherwise. A requested path is under [code]res://[/code], no longer than [constant MAX_REQUESTED_PATH_LENGTH], and ends in [code]tscn[/code] or [code]scn[/code]. [param path] is already resolved, so a [code]uid://[/code] reference is normalized by the caller that has the resolver.

method.name: resolve_requested_path
method.description: [method verify_requested_path] with the [ResourceUID] resolution in front of it, so a peer may name a scene by [code]uid://[/code] and still be bounded by the one rule. An empty [param reference] resolves to nothing rather than being handed to the resolver.

method.name: packed_at
method.description: The [PackedScene] a [code]res://[/code] path or [code]uid://[/code] reference names, or [code]null[/code]. A reference that resolves to nothing, or to a resource that is not a scene, answers [code]null[/code] rather than raising, because every caller here reaches a refusal code and none of them may take the session down with a bad path off the wire. This is the load, not the consent line: a path arriving from a peer clears [method resolve_requested_path] first.

method.name: packed_root_script
method.description: The [Script] on the root node of [param packed], read out of its [SceneState] rather than by instantiating it, so a scene's mark can be read before the session agrees to spawn it. A scene with no nodes, no root script, or a root [code]script[/code] property holding something else answers [code]null[/code].

method.name: scene_root_script_at
method.description: [method packed_root_script] of [method packed_at]. The one read a server does to learn what a requested scene declares about itself, and it costs a resource load and no instantiation.

method.name: destination_kind
method.description: What a scene destination [Variant] is, as one [enum Destination]. Every front door in the kit takes a destination loosely, and this is the single place that partition is decided, so the refusal a caller reports and the arm a caller takes come from one table. A [PackedScene] splits in two: [constant DESTINATION_PACKED] carries a resource path a peer can be told to load, and [constant DESTINATION_PACKED_UNPATHED] does not, which is the whole reason the refusal exists.

method.name: change_replaces_session
method.description: How far an admitted change reaches, as one answer: [code]true[/code] replaces the whole session and [code]false[/code] moves the one participant that asked. Three inputs decide it and this is the only place they meet, so the reach a capture takes and the reach a wire request takes cannot drift. A change with no participant to move names no smaller reach than the session, which is what authority's own front door asks for, so [param has_participant] being [code]false[/code] replaces the session whatever [member request_reach] says. [param declared_session_wide] arrives already decided, because the scene mark that answers it is the authoring tier's and stays GDScript, exactly as [param marked] does in [method native_change_strands].

method.name: native_change_strands
method.description: Whether a native scene change has left this peer out of the game. The session is intact either way: what strands the peer is a LOCAL change to a scene the session never agreed to, so an offline peer strands nobody and a marked scene is the change going through the front door. [param marked] arrives already decided, because the registry that answers it is the authoring tier's and stays GDScript.

method.name: move_verdict
method.description: Which of the three things a move into a destination can be. The caller resolves the destination only once this answers [constant MOVE_CARRY] or later, because resolving one activates a scene, and a move refused for a dead mover must not leave a scene standing that nobody arrived in. [codeblock] MOVE_REFUSED -> reject, no physics frame spent MOVE_ALREADY_THERE -> resolve OK, no physics frame spent MOVE_CARRY -> the awaiting branch: flush, reparent, flush [/codeblock] Refusal outranks arrival, so a mover that is nominally in a destination that is not live still refuses. [param same_scene] is only consulted once both ends are live.

method.name: admission_park
method.description: Parks [param peer] against [param scene], answering whether it parked. A peer admitted before the session holds a roster row for it has no participant to seat, so the admission is kept until the row lands. A scene that is not live parks nobody. A parked admission rides the live row rather than a book beside it, because the two open and close together and a peer parked against a scene that is gone must not be retried into it.

method.name: admission_unpark
method.description: Clears [param peer]'s parked admission on [param scene], answering whether one was standing.

method.name: admission_is_parked
method.description: Whether [param peer] is parked against [param scene], waiting for its roster row.

method.name: spawn_anchor
method.description: The node the next scene container is parented under: the declared anchor while it is alive, and [param fallback] otherwise. The caller passes the session root as [param fallback] rather than this class resolving one, so the decision is over its arguments and the ambient state stays outside it. This is the whole of the choice. A session that declared no anchor and a session whose anchor was freed answer identically, so a game that never mounts a declaration node keeps parenting under the root it always did, and losing a declaration node degrades to that same answer instead of dropping the spawn. [codeblock] anchor alive -> the anchor anchor freed or unset -> fallback, which may itself be null [/codeblock]

method.name: get_container_entered
method.description: The tree-entered half of [method set_container_lifecycle], or an invalid [Callable] when none was declared.

method.name: get_container_exited
method.description: The tree-exited half of [method set_container_lifecycle], or an invalid [Callable] when none was declared.

method.name: get_scene_anchor
method.description: The declared anchor while it is alive, and [code]null[/code] once it is freed. The read is what clears a freed anchor, so no caller has to unset one on behalf of a node that is already gone.

method.name: isolation_owns_world
method.description: Whether [param isolation], an [enum Isolation], asks a hosting peer for a scene of its own world. One reading of the value, so the container build and any policy that branches on isolation cannot disagree about which member means isolated.

method.name: set_container_lifecycle
method.description: Declares the pair [method NetwMultiplayerCore.scene_spawn_node] connects a new container's [signal Node.tree_entered] and [signal Node.tree_exited] to, each bound to the container. Held for the session the way [method set_request_handler]'s handler is, and cleared by neither [method clear] nor a re-host, because a registration outlives the scenes it will see. The constructor runs on every peer and is the only point that holds a container while it is still an orphan, so an edge not wired here is an edge that peer never sees. A pair left unset connects nothing rather than failing the spawn.

method.name: set_scene_anchor
method.description: Declares the node new scene containers are parented under. A declaration node pushes itself here as it installs its [NetwSceneConfig], so its scenes co-locate under it and tree order matches on every peer, and passes [code]null[/code] to give the anchor back. The anchor is held as an instance id and never as a reference, which is what lets a declaration node be freed without this class either crashing on it or keeping it alive. The last push wins, matching the one-instance-per-key rule the session's service registry follows, so two declaration nodes never contest the answer.

method.name: spawn_warns_shared_world
method.description: Whether a spawn now would put a second level into one physics space, which is [method would_share_one_world] read at the moment of a spawn. Nothing here refuses one: several shared-world scenes are legal since isolation became a per-scene fact, so this decides a warning and nothing else.

method.name: spawn_note
method.description: Says what [method spawn_warns_shared_world] found, once, naming [param stem], on the session's own log rather than the caller's.

method.name: unobserve
method.description: Reverses [method observe] for one [param callback]. Removing something never registered is inert rather than an error.

method.name: declaration_open
method.description: Begins a draft declaration carrying [param isolation] and [param level_spawn_function], discarding any draft still open. Nothing a draft holds is readable until [method declaration_publish], so a re-publish is never half visible: a reader between the two sees the previous declaration whole or none at all.

method.name: declaration_row
method.description: Adds one declared scene to the open draft: the [param stem] it answers to, the resource [param path] it instantiates from, the [param spawn_data] a custom constructor receives, and whether it is one of the scenes [param initial] to the session. [param spawn_data] is stored detached. An [Array] or [Dictionary] is deep-copied on the way in and again on the way out of [method declared_spawn_data], so the caller and this class never share one container and a later edit on either side is invisible to the other. Publishing an aliased row is the one way a declaration could change without anybody declaring it, and there is no path to it here. Naming a [param stem] twice merges into the row already drafted rather than doubling it: a non-empty [param path] and a non-nil [param spawn_data] overwrite, and [param initial] only ever turns on. An empty [param stem] declares nothing, and a row offered while no draft is open is dropped.

method.name: declaration_publish
method.description: Swaps the open draft in as the published declaration, in one act. Inert when no draft is open.

method.name: declaration_drop
method.description: Forgets the published declaration and any draft. Separate from [method clear], because a session that ends keeps what it was declared to be: the peer that re-hosts declared nothing new. Deregistering the declaration, or tearing the owning interface down, reaches here.

method.name: declaration_is_published
method.description: Whether a declaration has been published. This is what tells a configured session from a bare one, so an auto-declaration for a level dropped into the tree can defer to an explicit one.

method.name: declared_isolation
method.description: The isolation a declared scene takes when its own recipe names none, as an ordinal mirroring the [code]SceneIsolation[/code] enum this tier cannot see. Zero when nothing is published.

method.name: declared_level_spawn_function
method.description: The custom level constructor the declaration published, or an unset [Callable].

method.name: declares_scene
method.description: Whether the published declaration holds a row for [param stem].

method.name: declared_scene_path
method.description: The resource path declared for [param stem], or an empty [String] when no row names it or the row carries no path.

method.name: declared_spawn_data
method.description: The spawn data declared for [param stem], deep-copied, or [param fallback] when no row names it or the row declared none. A caller that hands the answer to a constructor and then mutates it cannot reach the declaration through it.

method.name: declared_initial_stems
method.description: The stems of the scenes declared initial, in the order they were declared, which is the order a starting session brings them online.

method.name: declared_scene_count
method.description: How many rows the published declaration holds. Zero when nothing is published.

signal.name: native_change_settled
signal.description: Emitted when a request that [method request_open] recorded as captured settles, on every outcome. A game that presented a loading screen when the native change was captured tears it down here, including when the request resolved [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] or [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_TIMEOUT] and no scene ever arrives. The settle and the announcement are one act, because two adjacent calls are two chances to send one without the other.

constants.constant: The entry names no scene file, so it can become no request. An in-memory instance reaches this, and the caller reports rather than desyncing.
A client detaches its local instance and asks server authority for the scene, which arrives as spawn frames.
Server authority replaces what the whole session presents, which is what a session-wide reach means when a scene is already live to replace.
A listen host presenting its own world reads the bare call as "move me", the same meaning a client's bare call carries, so it relocates rather than spawning a world it does not enter.
Server authority spawns the scene through the replicated pipeline. The default, because a change nobody narrowed is a scene the session gains.
The move cannot happen: either the mover is gone or there is no live destination to arrive in. The caller answers [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE].
The mover is already in the destination, so the move is complete before it starts. The caller answers [constant @GlobalScope.OK] without spending a physics frame.
A live mover is bound for a different live destination, and this is the ONE verdict whose caller awaits: the physics flushes either side of the reparent belong to this branch alone.
The value names no scene destination at all. The caller reports and does nothing, because there is nothing it could have meant.
A [String] or [StringName] naming a declared scene, resolved against the declaration rather than the filesystem.
A live scene node handed in directly. Whether it is still a scene the session holds is the caller's own reading, since this class is not the live book.
A [PackedScene] backed by a file, so its path is a thing every peer can be asked to load.

A [PackedScene] built in memory. It names nothing a second peer could load, so it is refused rather than activated: the scene would exist on one peer and the session would disagree about what is running.
The scene shares the session's world, and its container is a plain [Node].

A hosting peer builds the scene an offscreen [SubViewport] with its own world, so two live scenes never share a physics space. A peer that only views the scene still builds a plain [Node], because only the host simulates.
Admission changed for a participant. The subject is its peer id, not a handle: a participant is admitted before it has anything in the scene to point at.
A player entity entered or left. The subject is its entity [RID]. Every player also reports under [constant EVENT_ENTITY], so this is the narrower reading of one crossing rather than a second one.
Any tracked entity entered or left. The subject is its entity [RID]. Players report here too, so an observer wanting only them registers for [constant EVENT_PLAYER] instead of filtering.

The longest path [method verify_requested_path] will hand back. A bound rather than a limit anyone is expected to reach: a request arrives off the wire, and a length nobody checked is a length a peer chooses.

members.member: The scene this peer presents, or an invalid [RID]. Recomputed from [method resolve_current] rather than written by whatever changed, so a scene arriving, leaving or re-seating this peer all settle through one answer. Held rather than derived on read, because the readings it composes are the session's and this class holds neither of them.
The id [method open_request] will draw next.
The promise the request in flight will settle through, or [code]null[/code] when nothing is. Read-only by construction: see [method request_open].
The request currently in flight, or zero when none is. Read-only by construction: see [method open_request].

Suppresses the [method spawn_warns_shared_world] warning while a whole-session replacement is in flight. The incoming scene stands beside the ones it is about to replace for as long as the transition takes, and warning about that would fire on every scene change a session makes.

The single-owner policy door [method decide_request] asks first. An unset [Callable] is what restores the [method admits_request] consent line, so uninstalling is the same act as never installing. It survives [method clear], because it is a policy the game installed and not a record of the session that just ended.

How far an admitted scene request reaches, using the ordinals [code]NetwMultiplayer.SceneReach[/code] publishes: zero moves only the requesting participant, one moves the whole session. Server policy rather than something a requester may ask for. A reach outside the enum names nothing and is refused rather than stored for a later request to be measured against, so a write that does not take leaves the reach that was already in force. The ordinals are mirrored rather than bound, so [code]NetwMultiplayer.SceneReach[/code] stays the one published spelling.
